newsitem.title: CANADA: Freeze on Friedland's Inco lifted immediately.
newsitem.headline: Freeze on Friedland's Inco lifted immediately.

text.p: A freeze on US$152 million worth of Inco Ltd shares owned by international mining financier Robert Friedland will be lifted immediately, a spokesman for Friedland said Thursday.

An Ontario Court judge ruled this week that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency could not extend an injunction on the Friedland's Inco shares. The judge stayed his order until Friday to give the United States a chance to consider an appeal.
On Thursday, lawyers for the EPA sent Friedland's lawyers a letter confirming they would not seek a further stay.
"The United States will not be seeking a stay of the order," the letter said.

The EPA had argued that Friedland should be held responsible for environmental problems at a former gold mine he controlled in Summitville, Colorado. It requested an injunction on the shares until it could sue Friedland for US$152 million in costs to clean up the site.
Ontario Court Justice Robert Sharpe rejected the EPA's claim, calling its case "anything but clear."
The EPA has not yet decided whether it will seek an appeal, the letter said.
Friedland will be meeting with his lawyers to consider his next steps, his spokesman said from Vancouver.
